editorial:
Imagine being a rebellious teen who hates everything about your life, only to be shipped off to the middle of nowhere. That is exactly what happens to Sydney. After a few bad choices involving shoplifting and drinking, her mom decides she needs a change of scenery. You will see Sydney struggle as she moves in with her dad and his pregnant new wife, Emma. The vibe is very heavy on family tension at first, as Sydney feels like an outsider in her own father's new life. She misses her city friends and her boyfriend, making her feel completely alone in the quiet country air.

What really makes this story work is how Sydney forms a bond with Jess, a local girl who has gone through her own tragedy. The acting feels real, and the pacing is steady enough to keep you interested in the family's healing process. While it is a slower drama, the emotional payoff is worth it. If you enjoy heartwarming stories about broken families finding a way back to each other, you should check this out. It looks great if you can find a high-quality stream on Prime Video, but adding the Blu-ray to your collection is a great move for a cozy movie night.
endingExplained: Everything changes when the family gathers for the funeral of Sydney's grandfather. The shared grief forces everyone to stop fighting and actually talk to one another. Sydney finally opens up to her dad and accepts Emma as part of the family. By the end, the tension disappears, and Sydney finds peace with her new life in the country. She grows up a bit and realizes that family is more important than her city drama.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas and stories about growing up.
